title: Validation of Seismocardiography for Estimating VO₂max in Cardiac Patients
summary:
Study description:
The SEISMAX study is a prospective observational study to validate seismocardiography (SCG) as a method for estimating maximal oxygen uptake (VO₂max) in patients with cardiovascular diseases. The primary goal is to compare the accuracy of SCG-based VO₂max estimation with the reference values from cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET). Additionally, the study examines which demographic and clinical characteristics influence accuracy and evaluates the practicability of SCG measurement in routine clinical practice.
Participants are patients with coronary artery disease undergoing routine CPET. SCG measurements are performed in supine resting position before and after CPET. Data collection is pseudonymized; participation is voluntary and can be terminated at any time.
CPET is performed according to clinical standards, including continuous ECG and blood pressure monitoring. SCG measurement is conducted with the CE-certified VentriJect Seismofit® system and takes approximately 10–15 minutes, including preparation.
conditions: Patients diagnosed with coronary artery disease (ICD-10: I25); exact subdiagnoses are determined by cardiologists as part of routine clinical care.

interventions.name:
Observational group: Cardiac patients – SEISMAX group

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Written, dated and signed informed consent obtained after proper information has been provided
Diagnosis of coronary artery disease (CAD)
Preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF ≥ 50%)
Clinically stable health status
Planned routine spiroergometry at the Sport Cardiology Clinic Cologne (Dr. med. Jürgen Fritsch)
Exclusion criteria:
Acute cardiac events (e.g., myocardial infarction within the last 6 weeks)
Atrial fibrillation
Mechanical heart valve replacement
Heart failure (HFrEF, HFmrEF, HFpEF)
Implanted medical devices (e.g., pacemaker, implantable cardioverter-defibrillator [ICD] with pacemaker function) — participation only with individual physician approval
Heart surgery ≤ 3 months prior to study participation
Skin conditions or scars in the sternum area that could interfere with sensor placement
Severe comorbidities potentially affecting the cardiovascular system
Language or cognitive impairments preventing adequate information and participation
